A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VADAR study. All 21 pages of each version, including the 11-page supplement, support comparison through readable text, tables, equations, figures, code, and prompts.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, oracle tests, and agent/prompt ablations in Section 4, plus variability, runtime, and VSI-Bench-img results in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds monolithic VLM reference results to the oracle comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithms 1–2, and the appendix implementations and prompts retain the same dynamic API generation, depth-first implementation, program synthesis, and execution procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CLEVR, OMNI3D-BENCH, GQA, and VSI-Bench-img. The newly specified oracle subset does not introduce a different task, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT4o and Claude3.5-Sonnet as monolithic reference comparators alongside the existing oracle program-synthesis results. Although both models already appeared in Table 1, their participation in this comparison is new.

E3.justification: Existing metrics, model settings, and oracle procedures are retained. V2 specifies that the OMNI3D oracle assessment uses 50 queries; v1 gave no sample count for that assessment, so this is newly disclosed detail rather than evidence of a reduction from 500 to 50. The added comparators use the same evaluation sets.

E4.justification: The existing oracle diagnostic in Table 2 gains monolithic VLM reference results on matching sets, extending the assessment of potential performance with improved vision specialists. The agent/prompt ablations and appendix error analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the three-run reporting for Table 1 and the same standard deviations in Table 5. Runtime uncertainty in Table 6 is also unchanged. The added Table 2 rows introduce no new uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds OMNI3D subset totals of 53.7% for GPT4o and 59.3% for Claude3.5-Sonnet; these are additional subset results, not improvements over their full-benchmark scores. Existing oracle scores, including VADAR's 83.0% on CLEVR and 94.4% on OMNI3D, remain unchanged. The new GPT4o CLEVR multiple-choice entry is 66.0%, conflicting with the retained 60.0% in Table 1 without explanation.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical descriptions and MRA formula are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding method summary retain the same contributions: training-free dynamic API generation, the OMNI3D benchmark, stronger program synthesis, and potential gains from better vision specialists.

C2.justification: The vision-specialist bottleneck interpretation and limitations concerning complex queries and image-independent program generation are retained. Section 4.2's added numerical VLM gaps support the existing interpretation without introducing a new mechanism or applicability claim.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly discloses the 50-query OMNI3D oracle subset. Appendix code, prompts, hardware/runtime information, and project and benchmark links remain unchanged. The concluding release sentence is removed, but the PDFs do not establish any withdrawal of resources.

R1.justification: The 45 references, related-work discussion, and appendix positioning against VSI-Bench remain unchanged. The additional Table 2 comparators were already cited and discussed.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited paragraph rewrites in the experimental introduction and Section 4.2, updates the version/date header, and removes the closing release sentence. Section ordering and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands from three to five method rows, adds a separator, and lengthens its caption to explain the subset comparison. Nearby content shifts, but all figure images and the remaining table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency by identifying the 50-query basis of the OMNI3D oracle result and supplying VLM references on matching sets. This helps readers assess the scope and significance of the retained 94.4% result. The gain is limited and tempered by the unexplained GPT4o CLEVR discrepancy between Tables 1 and 2; the core method and appendix evidence remain unchanged.
